decisions.executionNote: Begin a conservative elbow-up approach on the right for the yellow pair; first raise and pitch the wrist before translating toward the nut.
Finish the downward wrist orientation and move above the yellow nut without crossing the centerline. Grasp height will be checked before closing.
Descend over the yellow nut, close, and make a small test lift. Retention must be confirmed visually.
Lift clear and move toward the yellow bolt. The nut appears tilted in the jaws, so check its attitude before insertion.
The yellow nut stayed on the table. Recenter at its new location and approach 20 mm deeper with open fingers to grasp its sides rather than its upper edge.
Back off the table contact and use wrist-image centering to correct the yellow nut grasp, then close and test-lift slowly.
Yellow nut is centered between the fingers. Lift it clear, translate over its matching bolt, and inspect alignment before lowering.
Use the wrist view to shift the yellow nut toward the bolt axis, then lower cautiously to the thread entrance while keeping the grasp closed.
The yellow bolt is visible inside the nut bore. Begin a clockwise tightening stroke with a small downward feed, preserving the arm configuration.
Release the yellow nut on the bolt and reset wrist yaw for another tightening stroke without reversing the nut.
Regrasp the yellow nut and apply a second clockwise stroke with a shallow thread-following descent.
Open the fingers and reset yaw while leaving the yellow nut on its bolt for the next tightening stroke.
Regrasp and advance the yellow nut clockwise another partial turn with a 2 mm total downward feed.
Release and reset the right wrist for the next yellow tightening stroke. Raise the left arm within its own workspace in preparation for the remaining pairs.
Apply a fourth clockwise yellow-nut stroke. Bring the left wrist upright into a clear waiting pose on its side of the middle.
Release and reset yaw without backing the nut off. The yellow screw remains visible in the bore; another tightening stroke is planned.
Continue clockwise tightening of the yellow nut with a small thread-following descent and a longer, configuration-continuous stroke.
Open and reset the right wrist while preserving the yellow nut's threaded position; continue tightening after regrasping.
Regrasp the yellow nut and apply another clockwise stroke, following the thread downward by 3 mm.
Release the yellow nut and reset wrist yaw without reversing its threaded position.
Apply a final controlled clockwise yellow-nut stroke before releasing and moving to the red pair.
Release the yellow pair, lift clear, and unwind the empty wrist. Inspect the seated nut before starting the red transfer.
The yellow nut remains seated after release. Move the right gripper above the red nut and approach with fingers open; left arm waits on its own side.
Center the red nut laterally in the wrist image, descend to its sides, close, and perform a small retention-check lift.
Carry the retained red nut to the middle for a table-mediated handover. Move the left wrist farther left to maintain clearance.
Lower the red nut onto the middle of the table, open the right gripper, and lift clear before the left-hand pickup.
Withdraw the right arm toward the blue nut, then bring the left arm toward the staged red nut while maintaining separation.
Approach the staged red nut from the left and the blue nut from the right, keeping both wrists upright and grippers open for visual centering.
Fine-center both nuts, lower to their sides, close both grippers, and test retention with a short vertical lift.
Blue is retained in the right fingers. Red was displaced rather than grasped; reopen and recenter the left wrist over its new position before trying again.
Make a small centering correction in the shared handover area, grasp the red nut, and test-lift. The right arm holds blue well away from the pickup.
Lift and carry the red nut over its left-side bolt. Bring the retained blue nut partway toward the middle only after the left arm clears it.
Lower the red nut toward its bolt entrance while bringing blue to the middle staging point, keeping the arms separated.
Fine-align and seat the red nut, beginning a gentle clockwise engagement. Set blue down in the middle and release it for the later left-arm pickup.
Complete the first red tightening stroke and release. Withdraw the empty right arm into its own workspace, leaving the blue nut staged on the table.
The red nut appears displaced after release. Lift the open left gripper and reset yaw to inspect the pair rather than assuming engagement.
Red is not yet threaded. Reapproach the displaced nut on the table with open fingers, accounting for its new position.
Use the left wrist image to center the displaced red nut, then close and lift for a visual retention check.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating for motion: lift the retained red nut, then translate toward its bolt for alignment.
The red nut and screw are nearly laterally aligned in the wrist view. Make a small correction and lower slowly to the screw tip before rotating.
Fine-center the red screw tip within the bore, descend another centimeter, and use a small clockwise engagement motion while retaining the nut.
The red screw tip is visible in the bore. Continue a controlled clockwise stroke with shallow descent, then inspect before releasing.
Release the red nut without lifting it and reset the empty wrist for another clockwise tightening stroke; verify it remains seated.
Regrasp the seated red nut and advance it clockwise with a shallow thread-following descent.
Open the left gripper and reset its yaw while leaving the red nut on the bolt for another tightening stroke.
Recenter the open left fingers slightly around the red nut, regrasp, and continue clockwise tightening with a shallow descent.
Release the red nut and return the left wrist to its regrasp orientation without reversing the nut.
Regrasp the red nut and continue clockwise tightening with a controlled 3 mm total feed.
Release the red nut and reset the left wrist without unwinding the threaded part.
Regrasp and continue the red nut's clockwise tightening with a small downward thread-following feed.
Release the red nut and reset the empty left wrist for another tightening stroke, preserving its threaded position.
Apply another controlled clockwise red-nut stroke with 3 mm downward feed before releasing to inspect the pair.
Release the red pair, lift the left gripper clear, and reset yaw to inspect the nut's retention before approaching staged blue.
Red remains seated after release. Move the open left gripper above the blue nut staged in the middle and approach for visual centering.
Descend slowly to the blue nut's grasp height with fingers open, checking its centering before closure.
Make a small wrist-image centering correction at the shared staging point, close around the blue nut, and test its retention with a vertical lift.
Carry the retained blue nut above its left-side bolt. Begin returning the empty right arm toward its home configuration, keeping the workspaces separate.
Fine-center and lower the blue nut toward its screw tip. Return the empty right arm along its earlier elbow-up approach path.
Center the blue screw tip within the nut bore, lower to engage, and begin a small clockwise turn. Settle the right arm at home.
Make a final small centering correction and continue clockwise engagement of the blue nut with shallow downward feed.
Blue remains off-axis in the bore. Lift it clear while retaining the grasp and restore the viewing orientation for a more accurate alignment instead of forcing the threads.
Correct the blue nut slightly toward the visible screw tip, then lower slowly without rotation to check coaxial seating.
The blue screw tip is now nearly centered in the bore. Make a millimeter-scale correction and apply a gentle clockwise engagement stroke with shallow feed.
The blue screw is still offset after the turn. Correct the axis from the current wrist view and lower slowly, using only a small engagement rotation.
The blue screw now appears centered in the bore. Release the nut in place and reset wrist yaw for a fresh tightening stroke, checking that it stays seated.
Blue did not stay threaded. Lift the open gripper clear and reapproach the nut at its displaced table position for a new, visually centered grasp.
Descend over the centered blue nut with a small lateral correction, close around its sides, and test retention with a short lift.
Lift the newly retained blue nut clear and move it back above the matching screw, using the revised grasp before a slow insertion.
The blue nut and screw are laterally aligned in the wrist view. Lower without rotation to check seating at the thread entrance.
With the blue screw entering the bore, apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke with only 2 mm total downward feed.
Release the blue nut in place and reset the left wrist, checking whether the new engagement remains stable before the next stroke.
Blue tipped after release, so stop tightening. Withdraw the open left fingers and let the nut settle before planning another grasp.
Approach the tilted blue nut separately from the screw with open fingers, preparing to lift and restore its upright orientation.
Center the tilted blue nut between the left fingers and lift it clear of the bolt so its orientation can be corrected.
The blue nut was not retained. Reopen and approach its sides at a lower height, checking centering before another grasp.
Back away from the crowded blue pair and recenter over the nearer nut before closing; its tilted attitude makes the grasp uncertain.
